subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Routine follow-up due to chronic medical conditions
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 61 years old, and I'm a male. I'm here for a routine follow-up because I have some chronic medical conditions, and I wanted to check in on how I'm doing overall. Doctor: Could you please specify what chronic medical conditions you have? Patient: I had an aortic valve replacement and an ascending aortic aneurysm repair back in 2013. Other than that, I don’t have any other chronic conditions that I’m aware of. I’ve been doing okay since then, but I wanted to make sure everything’s still on track. Doctor: Could you please describe any symptoms you have been experiencing since your aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair, such as chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or fatigue? Patient: I’ve been feeling more fatigued lately, especially after a long bike ride. I used to be able to ride 40 miles on a good day, but now I can only do 20 to 30 and I get really tired afterward. I also noticed that I purse my lips when I breathe, but I don’t have any wheezing or shortness of breath. Doctor: Have you undergone any recent echocardiograms or other cardiac imaging studies to assess the function of your aortic valve or the status of your ascending aorta? Patient: Yes, I had an echocardiogram recently, but I'm not sure exactly when. I think it was around September 2019, and I was told that everything looked okay. I wanted to make sure that the valve is still holding out since it's been eight years since my surgery. Doctor: Could you please provide the specific results of your September 2019 echocardiogram, particularly regarding the aortic valve function and the size of your ascending aorta? Patient: I don't have the specific results of the September 2019 echocardiogram with me, but I was told that everything looked okay at the time. I just wanted to make sure that the valve is still functioning well and that there haven't been any
